en.title: Integers Without Repeated Digits in a Range
en.description:
For each closed range of positive integers, count the integers whose decimal representation has no repeated digit. For the original example [9,84] the answer should be 69; the original 47 is wrong, and its list omits 84.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains q, followed by q lines of lower upper. Original bound 1≤q≤100000; the original upper bound on the endpoints is truncated, so this site adds 1≤lower≤upper≤1000000.
en.output: Output q lines of counts, one for each closed range in order.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 19 / 10; 2 / 26 / 69 / 8 / 4; 27. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Enumerate all positive integers without repeated digits (at most 6 digits) once and sort them; for each query, count the closed range with two binary searches.
